value.title: Cross-model review R1 (PAUSED pre-verdict) — 132-spawn-reports-bind
value.note: Read-only review of 132-spawn-reports-bind @ 3afa7def against main@4418e3f3. PAUSED before verdict at the PM's request (Jordan scope change: terminalize tombstoned OR pane-absent recipients, not only proc-null). Findings below are complete for the code as reviewed and are recorded so they survive the pause; R001 and R002 are merge blockers independent of the scope change. Fresh receipts taken by this reviewer, not the author: `cargo test -p pij-daemon -p pij-harnesses -p pij-cli` exit 0, 380 tests, 0 failed; `node_modules/.bin/vitest run .pi/extensions/pij/adapters/rust-runtime.test.ts` exit 0, 8/8; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` exit 101.

value.finding: CRITICAL. Registration overwrites the requested model with an ABSENT actual_model for every spawned seat, which both blanks a shipped field and turns a healthy Claude spawn into spawn.failed. `if binds_spawned_incarnation { descriptor.model = claim.actual_model.clone(); }` is unconditional, including when the claim carries None. The ONLY writer of actual_model in the tree is the pi/omp TypeScript extension (.pi/extensions/pij/adapters/rust-runtime.ts:345, fed by index.ts:373); `pij_cli::Registration` (crates/cli/src/client.rs:23) has no such field at all, so the CLI can never send it, and crates/daemon/src/claude_bind.rs:103 and crates/daemon/src/http/identity.rs:528 hardcode None. The Claude bind path IS claude_bind: `is_pending_spawned_claude` selects exactly harness==claude && proc.is_none() && pane.is_some() && spawn_id.is_some() — the same population the new wait loop watches — and registers with a MATCHING spawn_id, so binds_spawned_incarnation is true and model becomes None. Three consequences: (a) descriptor.model is destroyed, and bound_model (crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:1303, http/shim.rs:114, consumed by .pi/extensions/pij/cli.ts:1946) goes blank for every spawned Claude seat; (b) model_matches is false so NO spawn.bound event is published — G3 is unmet for the Claude harness; (c) launch_seat takes the mismatch branch and returns BAD_GATEWAY `model-mismatch: requested X, actual no-model` for a live, healthy, correctly-modelled seat. Timing is not marginal: the binder ticks every 5s (crates/daemon/src/lib.rs:589-590 with crates/core/src/config.rs:161 delivery_interval_secs = 5), well inside the 30s wait. The same root bites omp whenever ctx.model is undefined at session start (index.ts:373 emits undefined). Root cause is the classic collapse of ABSENT into a value: `no-model` is used to spell both `the client did not report` and `the client reported something different`, and only the second is a mismatch. Smallest fix: gate the override on `claim.actual_model.is_some()`, and treat an absent actual_model as unknown (neither match nor mismatch) in requested_model_matches and the wait loop.
value.receipt: Code trace above, plus the author's own test `spawn_reports_model_mismatch_without_killing_registered_seat` (crates/daemon/src/http/tests.rs) which ENSHRINES actual_model:None + a requested model => BAD_GATEWAY 'actual no-model'. Exhaustive writer check: `grep -rn --include='*.rs' --include='*.ts' -e actual_model -e actualModel .` returns exactly one non-test writer, rust-runtime.ts:345.

value.finding: HIGH. The branch cannot pass CI. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` exits 101 with `this function has too many arguments (8/7)` at crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:935 (`spawn_failure`, new on this branch). .github/workflows/ci.yml:102 runs that exact command, so this is a hard merge blocker, not style noise. It also means the composition step's 'harness checks' did not execute the gate CI executes — `just self-check` has no clippy target. Smallest fix: gather the evidence arguments (exit_code, reason, status, last_output, log_path) into one struct, or add a reasoned #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)].
value.receipt: Independently re-run by this reviewer, not taken from the PM's report: exit 101, single error, output at scratchpad/clippy.txt. Confirmed introduced by this branch (spawn_failure is added in the diff).

value.finding: HIGH — plan promise not true. G1 promises spawn returns {dispatched:true, bound:false|true, pane, pid} and reports bound OR a named failure. On the failure path — the exact path this plan exists to create — those structured fields do not exist. `spawn_failure` returns `Envelope::<SpawnResponse>::refused(...)`, and `Envelope::refused` (crates/core/src/model.rs) sets `data: None`. So every failure envelope carries dispatched/bound/pane/pid ONLY inside the human-readable `meta` prose string; a caller must regex prose to learn the pane or that dispatch succeeded. The author's own live-proof.md bad-model transcript shows exactly this: `{"ok":false,...,"meta":"spawn.failed: seat ... in pane %3068 ..."}` with no `data` key. Smallest fix: return ok:false WITH a populated data object (dispatched:true, bound:false, pane, pid:null) beside the error, so dispatch-vs-bind stays machine-readable in both outcomes.
value.receipt: crates/core/src/model.rs `Envelope::refused` sets data: None; docs/plans/132-spawn-reports-bind/assets/live-proof.md 'Dead/unusable model before honest bind' transcript.

value.finding: HIGH mechanism, severity graded down only for unknown usage frequency. The wait loop's sole bind evidence is `registry.get(id)` returning `proc.is_some()`, and the daemon runs exactly ONE binder — ClaudeBinder, Claude-only (crates/daemon/src/lib.rs:665). pi/omp self-registers through its extension. The codex harness has neither a binder nor an extension, so its pre-bind row keeps proc == None until an agent runs `pij register` by hand; after wait_seconds (default 30) spawn returns GATEWAY_TIMEOUT spawn.failed for a perfectly healthy seat. Because --wait is the DEFAULT (--no-wait is opt-out), this changes the default outcome for those harnesses from a true-but-weak 'dispatched' to a FALSE 'failed'. The whole feature was validated against the one harness that reports back. Smallest fix: make the timeout a non-error outcome (ok:false with dispatched:true/bound:false data, or ok:true with bound:false) rather than an adapter refusal, and/or default wait only for harnesses with a known bind path. Note copilot shares the mechanism but is retired per current fleet policy.
value.receipt: crates/daemon/src/lib.rs:665 is the only binder started; `ls crates/daemon/src/` shows claude_bind.rs as the only *_bind module; no codex/copilot registration writer found in the tree.

value.finding: MEDIUM — composition seam: the CLI re-derives the daemon's answer instead of consuming it. The daemon computes dispatched/bound/pid and serialises them in SpawnResponse (crates/daemon/src/http/types.rs, `spawn_success`). The CLI client deserialises into `Envelope<SeatDescriptor>`, silently DROPPING those three fields, then `spawn_cli_response` recomputes them from `seat.proc`. Two implementations of one fact either side of a wire, agreeing today by coincidence of identical logic and nothing else; and client-side `dispatched` is a hardcoded `true`, so the CLI structurally cannot ever report dispatched:false. The integration assertion in crates/cli/tests/spawn.rs reads json["data"]["dispatched"] and therefore proves the CLI's copy, not the daemon's. Smallest fix: deserialise SpawnResponse in the client and print what the daemon said.
value.receipt: crates/cli/src/main.rs `spawn_cli_response` maps Envelope<SeatDescriptor>; crates/daemon/src/http/types.rs SpawnResponse carries the same three fields.

value.finding: MEDIUM — AC1's receipt does not show what AC1 claims. AC1 reads: 'returns spawn.failed naming THE EXIT CODE and THE OMP LOG LINE THAT REFUSED'. Its cited receipt (assets/live-proof.md#deadunusable-model-before-honest-bind) shows `exit code unavailable` and `"exit_code": null`, and its last_output is the OMP status FOOTER (`⬢ no-model`), not a refusal log line — because the run took the model-mismatch branch, not the child-exit branch. Consequently G2 (capture the child exit code and last 20 lines when the pane exits before bind) has NO live receipt at all; it rests solely on the fake-tmux unit test spawn_wait_reports_child_exit_with_log_tail. Smallest fix: either restate AC1 to claim what was actually demonstrated (a live model-mismatch report), or produce a live run in which the child genuinely exits non-zero before bind.
value.receipt: docs/plans/132-spawn-reports-bind/assets/live-proof.md, both the pre-rebase and post-rebase bad-model transcripts, each showing exit_code null.

value.finding: MEDIUM residual — the terminal policy is IN the ruled scope, but it can permanently fail messages for a revivable seat. I verified the scope question the packet flagged: nothing in the daemon clears `proc` on a live seat — `proc: None` is written only at row creation (crates/core/src/model.rs:320; the only other hits are test fixtures) — so `recipient.proc.is_none()` really does mean 'never bound', and the policy is exactly the ruled proc-null case, not wider. The residual is that fail_claim is TERMINAL and the check does not require spawn_id.is_some(): in the window between a pane dying and `revive` writing the replacement row, any drain tick (every 5s) converts a recoverable queued message into a permanent Outcome::Failed, where the previous behaviour backed off and survived the revive. Smallest fix: skip terminalising while a revive is a live possibility for the seat, or scope the check to seats that were spawned and have never bound.
value.receipt: grep for `proc = None`/`proc: None` across crates/daemon/src and crates/core/src returns only model.rs:320 (constructor) plus two test lines; crates/daemon/src/pointer/worker.rs:208-231.

value.finding: NIT — spawn evidence files leak, and their location drifts from the plan. `spawn_evidence_paths` writes <spawn_id>.status and <spawn_id>.log under std::env::temp_dir()/pij-rs-spawn/. Only the success path removes the status file; the no_wait path removes neither, and `revive` now always passes no_wait: true, so every revive leaves two files behind permanently. G2 named ~/.pij-rs/spawn/<spawn_id>.log; temp_dir is a defensible substitute but the documented location no longer matches the code.
value.receipt: crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs spawn_evidence_paths and the `no_wait` early return; crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs revive_seat sets no_wait: true.

value.finding: Drift note, no revert requested. The impl-guide fences registration.rs to 'bind notification hook only'. Two changes exceed that: the parent-preservation change (`if let Some(parent) = claim.parent`) and the model override in R001 are both merge-logic behaviour changes, not the notification hook. The parent change is genuinely RED-witnessed (assets/red-witness.md, 'Spawn parent erased at bind') and fixes a real bug — I am flagging only that the fence was widened without an amendment, per the rule that a seam change is cheapest to rule on at the ack.

Friction report for the flowspace dogfood instruction (i1), not a defect in this branch. `flowspace3 doctor` reports ok and the production daemon was already up, so no daemon was started. Two misses: (1) the documented invocation `flowspace3 search "<q>" --mode semantic` is REJECTED by the shipped CLI (`error: unexpected argument '--mode' found`); only the bare `flowspace3 search "<q>"` form works, so any skill or memory carrying the --mode form is stale. (2) The index is stale relative to this branch: a semantic query for this plan's exact concept ('seat registration binds spawned incarnation model') returned plan-110 packet rows and no hit in crates/daemon/src/registration.rs, so consumer discovery for R001 had to be done with grep. Every finding above was located by reading the diff and by grep, not by flowspace.
value.receipt: flowspace3 doctor => ok; `flowspace3 search "..." --mode semantic` => 'unexpected argument'; bare search returned docs/plans/110-* rows only.
